name: Scarborough Bridge
facts: Scarborough Bridge, a timber town truss marvel, opened its wooden arches to traffic on February 14, 1959, honoring Bob Scarborough, the visionary developer behind Barclay Farm.
Designed by engineer Malcolm Wells, the bridge spans the North Branch, a modest tributary of the Cooper River, linking Covered Bridge Road to the rest of Cherry Hill.
Renovated in 1993, Scarborough Bridge remains a cherished historical landmark, proudly carrying two lanes of traffic alongside sidewalks for pedestrians and bicyclists.
